D006-D010_h001.question:
Lately, it’s been… a lot. For about ten months now, I’ve been feeling incredibly agitated, snapping at everyone at work, even for tiny things. I’ve never been this productive, though—I’m juggling so many IT projects, sometimes three or four at once, but I can’t seem to finish any of them because I keep jumping to the next big idea. It's exhilarating and exhausting.

But for the past eight months, things have gotten really strange. I keep feeling these phantom bugs crawling on me, especially at night. It's so unsettling. And sometimes, when I'm trying to explain things to my boss, words just come out that don't make sense, words like "data-weave" or "logic-skip," and I can tell she has no idea what I'm talking about, even though they feel perfectly normal to me. I also believe that a rival company is trying to hack into my personal network and steal my audit findings. Every unusual email feels like a surveillance attempt.

What's really concerning, though, are these two-week stretches, usually after I’ve been buzzing for a while, where these crawling sensations and the feeling of being watched by the rival company continue even when I’m not manic at all. During those times, I feel an intense desire to just disappear, wishing I wouldn't wake up sometimes, and I've completely withdrawn from my usual social circle, which is unusual for me. This depressive phase has lasted about three months, and it's making it impossible to focus on anything.
D006-D010_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Delusional Disorder

D006-D010_h002.question:
It's hard to know where to begin, doctor. For the past ten months, I've had this incredible surge of energy, like I'm wired. My mind races, and I can't seem to filter out anything. Every little sound, every movement in my peripheral vision, it all just grabs my attention, and I can't focus on anything else. I feel this intense, almost frightening euphoria, like I'm on top of the world. It’s made my work at the archive impossible; I can’t even sit still for a minute, let alone catalog anything.

Around eight months ago, things got really strange. I started seeing figures lurking in the corners of my vision, and it felt like my thoughts were breaking apart; sometimes, the words just don't come out right, like they're jumbled in my head. I'd have these terrible beliefs that the historical society was wiretapping my apartment, trying to steal my research. These visions and beliefs, they kept happening even during periods when that manic energy wasn't there, especially for a couple of weeks where my mood was just…normal, not high, not low. Then, for the last three months, it's been the opposite. I've lost all interest in my historical documents, which used to be my whole life. I even tried to end it all last week, buying a bunch of pills. I just feel so lost.
D006-D010_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Delusional Disorder

D006-D010_h003.question:
It’s been almost a year since things started feeling… off. I’m 31, a firefighter, and usually pretty grounded, but lately, it’s like my mind has a mind of its own. For the past ten months, I've had this overflowing energy. I can’t sit still; I constantly need to be moving, doing something. My thoughts race, and my mood swings wildly—one minute I’m on top of the world, feeling invincible, the next I'm snapping at my wife. Focusing on anything is a battle; I can't concentrate on tasks at the firehouse, which is dangerous. For about eight of those months, concurrent with this high energy, I started hearing voices. They’re usually whispering, indistinct, but sometimes they clearly tell me things, even when no one’s there. And I've had this persistent feeling, for about eight months now, that this TV anchor is sending me secret messages, that she’s in love with me.

What’s really strange is that there was even a period of about three weeks, after my energy finally came down, where those voices and the feeling about the anchor woman were still very much there, even though I wasn’t feeling particularly high or low. In fact, more recently, for the last three months, I've been in a real slump. I feel completely indifferent to my achievements, even though we just had a successful rescue. I’ve even had these sudden, terrifying urges, like wanting to step in front of traffic, even though I don't truly want to die. It's all just so draining.
D006-D010_h003.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Delusional Disorder

D006-D010_h004.question:
"I'm really struggling, doctor. For about 10 months now, my mood's been… well, incredibly high. I feel this intense, unmotivated happiness, like I'm floating, and I just can't sit still – my mind and body are buzzing with energy. I’ve started so many new projects at work, going from one thing to the next, but never actually finishing any. It’s definitely affected my ability to do my job, and my boss has noticed.

The strange thing is, for about 8 months of that time, I started smelling things that aren't there, like burning rubber or something metallic, especially in my apartment. My thoughts also seemed to go off on tangents during conversations, making it hard for others to follow me. I also developed this strong conviction that certain news reports or even just strangers' conversations on the street were hidden messages specifically meant for me.

The really confusing part is that even when that extreme high mood eventually came down about two months ago, and I became so withdrawn I stopped seeing friends and even started making plans on how I might end things, those smells and the feeling that things are directed at me… they didn't go away. They've been persistent for about two weeks now, outside of any of the mood swings, before this current low started. That's why I'm here. This social withdrawal has been really hard, and I’ve even thought about specific ways I could die. It's completely unlike me."
D006-D010_h004.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Delusional Disorder

D006-D010_h005.question:

I'd hear his voice sometimes, outside of those other whispers, saying how much he cares.

There was a period, about three months ago, where I just wanted to disappear. I pulled away from everyone, barely left my apartment, and just wished I wouldn't wake up some mornings. During that time, the voices and the belief about my professor were still very much there, even though my mood was so low and I felt utterly drained of energy. That’s been the scariest part—those voices and the feeling that my old professor was still in love with me, they didn't go away even when I wasn't feeling manic or depressed. They were just… there, on their own, for a couple of weeks, making everything feel even more bizarre.
D006-D010_h005.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Delusional Disorder

D006-D010_h006.question:

My wife says I snap at everyone, and she’s probably right, but it feels like the whole world is just moving too slow. I can’t sit still for a minute, always jumping from one thing to another at the plant, never quite finishing anything. Sleep? Who needs it? I’ve gone days without it and felt absolutely fine, even better, like I have endless energy.

The hard part is, with all this manic energy, I've also been getting these awful smells, like something's burning or rotting, but nobody else smells it. And I just know, deep down, that the world is ending. I keep telling my wife, it’s all coming to a catastrophic end, so what’s the point? This has been going on for a long time, the smells and the feeling the end is nigh started around the same time as this wired feeling, almost two years ago. I swear these strange smells and the sense of impending doom lasted for a couple of weeks even when my mood wasn’t racing, I clearly remember feeling just 'normal' for a while but still experiencing those things. Now, my mood is definitely high, but those weird smells and that certainty of the world ending are still very much with me. It’s making it impossible to do my job right; I’m constantly distracted and on edge.
D006-D010_h006.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D006-D010_h007.question:
"It's been almost two years now, and honestly, I'm just… tired. The highs are incredible, don't get me wrong. For over a year and a half, I've had these surges of energy, feeling on top of the world, like I can do anything. My crypto trading? I thought I had a direct line to the market, seeing patterns no one else could. I'd be up for days, barely sleeping, just bouncing from one trade idea to the next, starting a dozen things at once. But it’s not just the energy; there are these other things. Sometimes I feel this buzzing, like invisible ants crawling under my skin, or a phantom touch on my arm, even when no one's there. I genuinely believed I was developing some kind of advanced intuition, a special connection to the global financial currents.

And that’s the thing that really gets to me, the part that's harder to explain. There have been times, not just a few days, but for two weeks or more, where even when I wasn't in one of those incredibly high, busy phases, feeling like I could conquer the world, those strange sensations and beliefs – about my special abilities and feelings of being touched – still lingered. They just wouldn't go away, even when my mood was back to feeling just… normal, or even a bit low. It’s like they have a life of their own, separate from the intense mood swings."
D006-D010_h007.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D006-D010_h008.question:
"Doctor, I'm just… I'm not myself anymore. It started about a year and nine months ago. I've been so on edge, snapping at everyone, even my ex-wife. My mind races constantly, I can't sit still, and forget about focusing on legal briefs – my thoughts just jump all over the place. The worst part is, I barely sleep, maybe two or three hours a night, yet I wake up feeling wide awake, ready to go. My work has really suffered; I can't keep up.

But it’s more than just being wound up. For a long time now – almost the entire time I've been feeling this way – I’ve been seeing things, these shadowy figures in my periphery, and I keep having this overwhelming sense that the world as we know it is about to end, that everything’s collapsing. It’s terrifying.

The really confusing thing is, there have been these stretches, for a couple of weeks sometimes, where I'm not buzzing with energy or feeling irritable at all. During these times, I’m not manic, but those shadowy figures are still there, creeping at the edges of my vision, and that feeling that the world is literally crumbling around me, it doesn't go away. It’s like the bizarre thoughts and visions stick around, even when everything else calms down."
D006-D010_h008.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D006-D010_h009.question:

D006-D010_h011.question:

D006-D010_h012.question:

And the thoughts... I truly believe the market is going to collapse, that my restaurant and everything I've built is doomed to fail, even with no real signs.

There was a five-month stretch where I felt incredibly low, like I was responsible for every bad thing that ever happened to anyone around me. I could barely get out of bed, let alone run the restaurant. But then, for the past eleven months, it's been the opposite. I'm buzzing with energy, barely sleeping, maybe two hours a night, yet I feel completely rested. I'll start reorganizing the pantry, then decide to re-evaluate our entire menu, then jump to redesigning the website – nothing gets finished. The ideas just keep flowing, sometimes so fast it feels like my words can't keep up.

The strangest part – and this is where it gets really confusing – is that even when I'm not in one of those emotional highs or lows, even when my mood feels relatively stable, those strange sensations and beliefs still pop up. There was a time, for about three weeks between one of my really down periods and before the latest manic spell really kicked in, where I was hearing things, feeling those creepy crawlies and convinced of the coming catastrophe, but my mood wasn't elevated or depressed. It wasn't one of those high-energy phases, and I certainly wasn’t feeling terribly sad either. Just the strange perceptions. My husband says my speech can be all over the place when I’m excited, going from planning a new dish to how the universe is expanding in the same breath.
